text:
Situation: Lorazepam injection has been on FDA's shortage list since 2018-05-03 and remains current as of 2026-10-21. Current inventory provides 3.4 to 38.2 days of supply across formulations and sites.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the shortage on 2018-05-03. The label for NDC 00409-1985-30 names Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1925262) as the manufacturing plant. FDA inspection 976095 at that plant ended 2016-06-08 and was classified OAI, 694 days before the shortage posting. A Warning Letter was issued to the same plant on 2017-02-14, 443 days before the posting. A later inspection 1064827 ended 2018-08-15 and was also classified OAI, with the classification letter dated 2020-04-22.

Our position: Supply is critically low for injection products. Tablet inventory is adequate for the near term. The rule-identified best option is to buy from Civica, Inc., which is not on FDA's shortage list today.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to initiate purchase from Civica, Inc. (not on FDA shortage list). Requires buyer approval.
2. Buyer to evaluate purchase from REMEDYREPACK INC. (not on FDA shortage list). Requires buyer approval.
3. Pharmacist to verify and implement Hikma Pharmaceuticals USA Inc. 2 mg/mL formulation per existing approval by Riley Brooks, PharmD (2025-12-01). Requires pharmacist approval.
4. Pharmacist to verify and implement Hospira, Inc. 2 mg/mL formulation per existing approval by Alex Morgan, PharmD (2026-05-04). Requires pharmacist approval.

Not recommended: No clinical dosing changes or therapeutic substitutions at this time. Those decisions rest with treating clinicians and the committee.
